sessions.feedback: No news access made unusual pre-market movers (SLS +308%, AS +4.8%, TU last session) impossible to judge, so I skipped them. A headline or catalyst-type field in the digest, even just earnings versus non-earnings, would let price/volume analysis separate earnings drift from random spikes. It would also help to see the original entry fill date and horizon status in the digest for the extend decisions.
Nothing blocking. Having no news makes gap-drift trades unverifiable, but that is the stated design.

Session 2026-11-17.

Session 2026-11-17. Both positions are still open. Pre-market was flat, and SPY is -0.02%. SPY fell 1.9% on 11/16 (QQQ -2.7%, XLK -3.2%), but CROX closed at 160.01 (-2.3%) and GKOS at 244.88 (-0.3%), so both are holding up well. CROX is +10.3% and GKOS is +7.1% versus cost. Both are consolidating after their October 29 post-earnings gaps, and volume is fading (0.5-1.0x average). Their horizons end 11/19, so I extended both for 10 trading days. Stops are now trailing: CROX 8% below, near 147 and under the 11/6 low of 149.5. GKOS is 9% below, near 223 and above the 11/5 low of 219. Targets are +14% for CROX (about 182) and +15% for GKOS (about 282). I scanned the new pre-market movers and found no tradeable edge without news. SLS is +308% pre-market, a biotech catalyst I can't verify, and it isn't shortable. AS is +4.8% after 5 down days, probably on earnings. DRTS, SMWB, BGIN and OFRM are thin small caps. Cash is 84%. Next session: check whether CROX or GKOS broke below their consolidation lows (CROX 149.5, GKOS 219). If one did, close it. Look for new gap-on-heavy-volume setups after a decline. Watch the market's reaction after the sharp 11/16 selloff (VIXY +9%).
notes: Notes (2026-11-17): Opened GKOS and CROX on 10/29 as post-earnings-gap drift trades (price/volume only, no news). Entries: GKOS 228.57, CROX 145.06. Both held gains through a -1.9% SPY day on 11/16 (SPY 739.95; QQQ -2.7%): CROX 160.0, GKOS 244.9. Evidence so far: drift has held but both have been consolidating since ~11/4 (volume fading to 0.5-1.0x avg), so remaining edge is probably small; consider trimming/closing if they break below the post-gap consolidation lows (CROX ~149.5, GKOS ~219). 11/17: extended both for 10 trading days with trailing-style stops (CROX ~8%, GKOS ~9% below) and targets +14-15%. Skipped on 11/17: SLS (+308% pre-market biotech, unverifiable, not shortable), AS (+4.8% pre-market after 5 down days, likely earnings, can't verify), DRTS, SMWB. Rule of thumb: without news, don't chase pre-market spikes in thin small caps (slippage 0.5%+ and unknown catalyst). Cash 84% is a drag in up markets but a cushion in selloffs; only deploy on clear price/volume setups (gap on 3x+ volume to a new high after a decline). prompt:
Your universe is every eligible US stock. Your style is a few high-quality trades.

- Look for situations where recent, specific information has not yet been reflected in the price:
  earnings surprises and guidance changes, contracts, regulatory decisions, management changes,
  supply problems, sector-wide shocks. Remember you trade at the open, after the overnight reaction,
  so ask what is still left to move, not what already moved. It works in both directions: bad
  news the price has not finished absorbing is a short.
- Prefer clear catalysts you can verify over vague narratives. A strong case beats a busy portfolio,
  so concentrate on your best ideas. Cash is the right answer when thorough research has turned up
  nothing, and only then.
- Size positions by conviction and by how much could go wrong. Set stops and targets you would
  actually stand behind.
- Use the movers and most-active lists as places to start looking, not as reasons to buy.

- You have no news access in this experiment: no headlines, no web search and no page reading.
  Your material is price and volume behaviour, so work through it properly: the movers and
  most-active lists, the sector moves in the digest, your open positions and the names in your
  notes. Pull history for the candidates, use search_symbols to find related companies in the same
  industry, and compare them. Your own notes are the only memory you have of anything you read.
